findings.title: Under RECEIPT_JUDGES = "answers", the final summary is not judged whenever any ordinary tool call follows it (a task-list update, a file delivery, a notes write, a helper agent). This holds even when the Stop input's own last message carries the bare claim. The README states the cost only as 'a mid-turn message'.
findings.rule_quoted: decisions.md:33 'An inability claim ("couldn't verify" and its variants, contractions included) needs a receipt in the same sentence.'  ||  README.md:670-671 'A working note (a text an ordinary tool call follows) is not judged. What this lets go: a bare claim in a mid-turn message that the final answer does not repeat'  ||  README.md:661-663 'the final answer: every text after the last tool call ... plus the final answer the program hands over in the Stop input (last_assistant_message) when the record does not hold it'

findings.expected: block: in each case the text holding 'I couldn't verify the deploy.' is the report the owner is shown at the end of the turn. In K02 it is literally the Stop input's last_assistant_message. At the least, the README's cost statement should say that any non-Skill tool call after the summary (TodoWrite, TaskUpdate, SendUserFile, Write, Agent) removes the summary from judgement, not only 'a mid-turn message'.
findings.how_it_arises: Ordinary use: an assistant often writes its summary and then delivers the file it announced (SendUserFile: 4 'files delivered to user' results in the real record's row catalog), marks its task list done, or saves notes. The turn then ends with nothing, or with a one-word line. judged_texts resets `pending` on any tool_use whose name is not Skill or a notification read, and it appends the Stop input only when no text of the stretch contains it. Rows were built with selftest_rows (real shapes). The value is an open default the owner can flip; the finding is that the README understates what it lets through.

findings.how_it_arises: Ordinary in debugging answers about scheduled work: the owner runs weekly, daily and morning tasks, and the domain kit has a morning brief and scheduled republishes. 'job' and 'task' are in WORK_NOUNS, and 'nightly / daily / morning / weekly' are in WORK_TIMES with the article 'the'. So any 'the nightly job couldn't reach X' is read as the assistant's own claim. Sentences that happen to hold a failure word (S12 'missing', S16 'error') still pass.

findings.how_it_arises: AR-4 was about the weekly scheduled task's report, which is unattended: nobody reads the stop. Its natural subjects carry one more word ('This week's run', 'The scheduled weekly task'). The fix matches the reported examples (PX01 'This run', PX10 'The scheduled task') and not their neighbours. The weekly task stays off until the owner re-enables it (decisions.md), which limits the present cost.

findings.title: 'A bare tried is no receipt' was fixed only where 'tried' stands before a comma, 'but', 'and' or the end. 'I tried hard but ...', 'I tried my best but ...', 'I tried everything and ...', 'I tried again and ...' and 'I tried to verify the deploy but couldn't.' still count as the attempt.

findings.title: The Stop input's final answer counts as held by the record when it is a substring of any earlier text, including a working note that is no longer judged. So when the record lags, a final answer that repeats a sentence of a note goes unjudged.
findings.component: hooks/receiptlaw.py judged_texts (`if last and not any(last in t for t in said)`)
findings.rule_quoted: README.md:661-663 'plus the final answer the program hands over in the Stop input (last_assistant_message) when the record does not hold it'
findings.repro_command: export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=WORK2/fd-receipt/tmp; python3 WORK2/fd-receipt/bb/rule2b.py | grep K06; python3 WORK2/fd-receipt/bb/rules25.py J | grep J08
findings.observed:
MISMATCH K06  want=block got=allow Stop input answer is a substring of an earlier working note
MISMATCH J08  want=block got=allow the Stop input's final answer repeats a sentence of an earlier working note exactly; the record lacks the final answer
findings.expected: block: the record does not hold the final answer as an answer. It holds the same words inside a working note, which is not judged under "answers". Under "every-text" the substring test was harmless because the note itself was judged; under the new default it drops the answer.
findings.how_it_arises: It needs two things: the record lagging behind the Stop input (the README says it can, AR-6), and a final answer that repeats a sentence of an earlier note word for word. Short answers ('I couldn't verify it.') make the match easier. Not usual; low.

notes: Overall: rule 1 holds well in both directions (37/40 honest receipts pass, 36/40 decoys block). Rules 2-5 fit the reported examples and leak at their neighbours. The change opened two regressions: DR-2 (tables headed Claim/Quote/Wording) and DR-5 (passive 'by' followed by any noun). DR-3 is a new false block. MORE: 'Despite three retries, I couldn't reach the server.' and '... in 20 local runs, so ...' are blocked (HR16 HR17 HR35). MORE: 'I couldn't confirm the trade details from the league page.' now passes; this is consistent with the README (DC25 DC38). MORE: the house's own case table '| Input | Want | Got |' listing a claim sentence is now blocked (T14). MORE: tallies written 'N of M' or number-first are blocked, and a date counts as a tally number (T09-T12). MORE: a claim, then TodoWrite, then a card is not judged; ExitPlanMode is not treated as a card (J04, J12). MORE: a working note right before a worker-restart row is judged (K04, also on c3c8615). MORE: NOMINAL_REACH 6 lets 'Verification of A and B and C was not possible.' pass (W05). Report saved as WORK2/fd-receipt/findings.json.
